title: First-time offender leniency in NDPS - myth or reality
p1:
First time caught under NDPS law? Many believe the law gives an automatic second chance. But the reality is more complicated.

A common assumption is that a person with no past record will easily get leniency in a drug-related case. That is not always true.
p2:
Under the NDPS Act, being a first-time offender by itself does not guarantee release, a lighter punishment, or the dismissal of charges. Courts look at several factors, including the type and quantity of the substance, the evidence available, and the circumstances of the case.

One surprising point: the law treats the quantity involved as a major factor. A small quantity case and a commercial quantity case can lead to very different legal outcomes, even for someone with no previous record.
p3:
The practical takeaway is simple: 'first offence' can be a factor considered by a court, but it is not a magic shield against NDPS consequences. Every case depends on its own facts, evidence, and legal position.

Knowing this difference can prevent dangerous assumptions and misinformation.
conclusion: Do you think first-time offenders under NDPS should receive automatic leniency, or should the nature of the offence matter more?
